speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have some concerning symptoms, so I need to ask a few questions to help figure out what is going on. When did you first notice the yellowing of your skin and eyes, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools, and do you have any pain in the right upper quadrant of your abdomen? REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests, Hepatitis Panel, CBC

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal hepatitis panel and your history of substance use, have you been taking any over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or herbal supplements recently? I also need to know if you have experienced any confusion, sleepiness, or difficulty coordinating your movements.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you take any acetaminophen or other medications in the days leading up to these symptoms, and have you experienced any confusion or changes in your sleep-wake cycle? I need to rule out toxic liver injury and assess for hepatic encephalopathy. REQUEST TEST: Serum Acetaminophen Level, Ammonia Level

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal acetaminophen and ammonia levels, I need to explore other causes of acute liver injury. Have you consumed any wild mushrooms or herbal supplements in the past week, and have you noticed any joint pain or rash? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Liver Panel, Ceruloplasmin, Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Autoimmune Liver Panel: NORMAL READINGS, Ceruloplasmin: 15 mg/dL (low), Abdominal Ultrasound: Normal hepatic parenchyma, no signs of cirrhosis or mass

speaker: Doctor
text: Your low ceruloplasmin levels suggest Wilson's disease, so have you noticed any tremors, difficulty speaking, or changes in your handwriting? I also need to check for copper deposits in your eyes. REQUEST TEST: Slit-lamp eye exam, 24-hour urine copper

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Slit-lamp eye exam: Kayser-Fleischer rings present, 24-hour urine copper: Elevated

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Kayser-Fleischer rings, low ceruloplasmin, and elevated urine copper in the context of acute liver failure confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's disease
